findings.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — Case-sensitive email matching without normalization allows blocked addresses to bypass the check when stored and submitted addresses differ in case.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:17 — Statistics updates occur within the User#save transaction and roll back when validation rejects a blocked email, preventing match_count and last_match_at from persisting.
app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — Incrementing match_count through a non-atomic read-modify-save sequence loses updates during simultaneous checks.

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:17 — Statistics updates occur within the User#save transaction and roll back when validation rejects a blocked email, preventing match_count and last_match_at from persisting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) which updates match_count and last_match_at via record.save. This happens during validation phase. However, the save in should_block? is a separate database operation on the BlockedEmail model, not part of the User model's transaction. When User validation fails, it doesn't roll back because the BlockedEmail.save already committed independently. The finding assumes these are in the same transaction, but they're not - BlockedEmail.should_block? does its own save which commits immediately. The User model validation failure doesn't affect the already-committed BlockedEmail update.
